meaning: Something that appears bad or unlucky at first, but results in something good
hindi: प्रत्यक्ष बुरा, परन्तु वास्तव में अच्छा
example: Losing that job was a blessing in disguise — he found his true passion afterward.

meaning: Avoid coming to the main point; talk about something indirectly
example: Stop beating around the bush and tell me what you want.

meaning: Endure a painful or difficult situation with courage
hindi: कठिन परिस्थिति को साहस से झेलना
example: He bit the bullet and underwent the surgery without complaint.

meaning: To initiate conversation in an awkward situation; ease tension
example: He told a joke to break the ice at the new office.

meaning: To work or study late into the night
example: She burned the midnight oil to prepare for the exam.

meaning: Speak plainly and frankly without mincing words
example: He always calls a spade a spade, even if it offends people.

meaning: To discover someone in the act of doing something wrong
hindi: किसी को गलत काम करते पकड़ना
example: The thief was caught red-handed by the security guard.

meaning: Raise a false alarm; give a false warning
example: He cried wolf so often that no one believed him when danger was real.

meaning: Do something in the easiest way, often sacrificing quality
hindi: काम को आसानी से करना, चाहे गुणवत्ता जाए
example: The contractor cut corners and built a substandard building.

meaning: A person who is unknown but wins unexpectedly
example: The dark horse candidate won the election by a landslide.

phrase: Every cloud has a silver lining
meaning: Every difficult situation has a positive aspect
hindi: हर मुसीबत में कुछ अच्छा होता है
example: Though she failed the exam, every cloud has a silver lining — she learned from her mistakes.

meaning: Accept the consequences of one's actions
example: He finally had to face the music after years of dishonesty.

phrase: Hit the nail on the head
meaning: Describe exactly what is right or true
example: You hit the nail on the head with that analysis.

phrase: Kill two birds with one stone
meaning: Accomplish two things with a single action
example: By visiting both cities on the trip, she killed two birds with one stone.

phrase: Let the cat out of the bag
meaning: Accidentally reveal a secret
example: He let the cat out of the bag about the surprise party.

meaning: Lose an opportunity by being too late
example: He missed the boat on that investment and lost a fortune.

meaning: Undecided or neutral about something
example: She was still on the fence about accepting the offer.

meaning: Very rarely
example: He visits his hometown only once in a blue moon.

meaning: To tease or joke with someone
example: Don't take him seriously — he's just pulling your leg.

meaning: Suspect that something is wrong or dishonest
hindi: कुछ गड़बड़ होने का शक होना
example: She smelled a rat when the deal seemed too good to be true.

meaning: Reveal secret information by accident
example: Who spilled the beans about the surprise?

phrase: The ball is in your court
meaning: It is now your responsibility to take the next step
example: I've done my part — the ball is in your court now.

meaning: Feeling ill or unwell
example: He couldn't attend the meeting as he was feeling under the weather.

meaning: Uncertain or not yet decided
example: Our holiday plans are still up in the air.

meaning: A way of asking what someone is thinking about
example: You've been quiet all day — a penny for your thoughts.

meaning: Make a bad situation worse
example: His angry reply only added fuel to the fire.

meaning: Looking for something in the wrong place or blaming the wrong person
example: If you think I took your pen, you're barking up the wrong tree.

phrase: Bite off more than you can chew
meaning: Take on more responsibility than you can handle
hindi: अपनी क्षमता से अधिक काम लेना
example: She bit off more than she could chew by managing three projects at once.

meaning: Keep changing one's attitude or opinion
example: He kept blowing hot and cold about joining the new company.

meaning: Do something that cannot be undone; cut off all means of retreat
hindi: पीछे लौटने का रास्ता बंद करना
example: By quitting so abruptly, he burned his bridges with the firm.

meaning: Win or be successful
example: The team's excellent strategy carried the day.

phrase: Costs an arm and a leg
meaning: Very expensive
example: That designer dress costs an arm and a leg.

meaning: Argue or fight with someone
hindi: किसी से लड़ना या बहस करना
example: The two leaders often crossed swords in parliament.

meaning: Fail to recall something; get no result
example: When asked for the answer, he drew a blank.

meaning: Make a mistake; fail to do something correctly
example: He dropped the ball on the most important assignment.

meaning: An achievement to be proud of
example: Winning the national award was a real feather in her cap.

meaning: Lose control
example: The protest got out of hand and turned violent.

meaning: Ignore or be unfriendly to someone deliberately
example: After the argument, she gave him the cold shoulder.

phrase: Go back to the drawing board
meaning: Start over again from the beginning after a failure
example: The plan failed, so they went back to the drawing board.

meaning: To study intensely
example: He hit the books every night before the exam.

meaning: Go to bed
example: I'm exhausted — I'm going to hit the sack early tonight.

meaning: In trouble
example: He landed himself in hot water after missing the deadline.

meaning: Follow a trend; do something because everyone else is doing it
example: Many companies jumped on the bandwagon after the app became popular.

meaning: Prevent something from coming too close
example: Regular exercise can keep illness at bay.

meaning: Die
example: The old farmer finally kicked the bucket at age 92.

meaning: Try every possible option to achieve something
example: She left no stone unturned in her search for the missing child.

phrase: Make a mountain out of a molehill
meaning: Exaggerate a minor problem
example: Stop making a mountain out of a molehill — it's just a small scratch.

phrase: Not judge a book by its cover
meaning: Not judge people or things by appearance alone
example: Don't judge a book by its cover — he may look rough but he's kind-hearted.

meaning: Something very easy
example: The maths paper was a piece of cake for her.

meaning: Change one's behaviour for the better
example: After his arrest, he decided to turn over a new leaf.
